what: The Overtime Calculator works out your pay for a week that includes overtime. It splits your hours into regular, overtime and double time, multiplies each by the right rate, and adds them up.
You can enter weekly totals if you already know your overtime hours, or enter each day and let the tool apply daily and weekly limits for you.
uses: Make sure overtime was paid correctly.
See how much a few extra hours are worth.
See what different overtime rates mean in money.
Project a typical week across a month and a year.
tutorial: Pick your currency and type your "Normal hourly pay".
Type "Regular hours", "Overtime hours" with its rate, and "Double-time hours" with its rate.
Type the hours for Monday to Sunday and set "Overtime after (hours per week)" and, if they apply, daily overtime and double-time limits.
See total pay, regular pay, overtime pay, double-time pay, total hours and your average per hour.
The table shows the same week across two weeks, a month and a year.
features: Use 1.5, 2 or any rate from 1 to 10.
Daily limits are applied first, then the weekly limit.
Shows what you really earned per hour including overtime.
Week, two weeks, month and year.
Your last entries and mode come back next time.

example.title: Worked example
example.text: At 20 an hour you work 40 regular hours, 5 overtime hours at 1.5× and 4 hours at 2×. Regular pay is 40 × 20 = 800, overtime is 5 × 30 = 150 and double time is 4 × 40 = 160, for a total of 1,110 over 49 hours, about 22.65 per hour on average.

tips: Check your contract or local labour rules for the exact limits and rates.
Paid breaks and holidays may count differently; follow your employer's rules.
Use "Day by day" when long days trigger overtime even in a short week.
Copy the summary to compare with your payslip.
problems: A message says a day has only 24 hours
One day has more than 24 hours. Fix that day.
The daily double-time limit must be higher than the daily overtime limit.
Check the overtime rates are multipliers (1.5), not amounts.
